blurb: Small white companion dog from Madagascar with a soft, cotton-like coat
description: The Coton de Tulear is a small companion dog from Madagascar with a soft, fluffy, cotton-like white coat, a curled tail and a lively, merry expression.
answer: The Coton de Tulear is a small Bichon-type companion dog named for the port of Tuléar (Toliara) in Madagascar, where it is the national dog. It stands about 22 to 30 cm tall and usually weighs around 3.5 to 6 kg. It is known for its cotton-like coat and is traditionally described as lively, bright and merry.

body: The Coton is of Bichon type, most closely linked to the Bichon Tenerife. Its ancestors may have reached Madagascar on ships in the 16th and 17th centuries, and one story tells of small white dogs swimming ashore after a shipwreck. It was a companion of the Merina, Madagascar's ruling group, and is not a hunting dog. The French kennel club recognized it in 1970 and the FCI published its standard in 1972. Robert Jay Russell, who brought the first dogs to America in the 1970s, called it the Royal Dog of Madagascar, and the AKC fully recognized it in 2014.

The Coton has soft, medium-to-long hair compared to a cotton ball, a prominent black nose, large round dark eyes often covered by bangs, somewhat short legs, and a tail carried over the back. Accepted colors include white, black and white, and tricolor, and many puppies fade toward white as they mature. The FCI standard calls for a mainly white coat.
The expression is traditionally described as lively, intelligent, bright and merry. The breed is described as small and friendly, with very little prey drive.

Matting is common, so daily brushing and combing is advised, and grooming can be a challenge. The coat is described as low-shedding with low dander and is often called hypoallergenic. Its long back and short legs increase strain during jumping, stairs or sudden turns.

The available sources name few specific health conditions in the breed. Breed clubs generally recommend health screening of breeding stock and regular veterinary check-ups. A 2024 UK study of 44 dogs found a life expectancy of 14.2 years.

faq.a: The Coton is described as a non-shedding, low-dander breed, though puppies may shed their puppy coat and the adult coat needs daily brushing.

faq.q: How long do Coton de Tulears live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study of 44 dogs found a life expectancy of 14.2 years.

faq.q: How big does a Coton de Tulear get?
faq.a: It typically stands about 22 to 30 cm tall and weighs around 3.5 to 6 kg, with males larger than females.

faq.q: Is the Coton de Tulear recognized by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI published its breed standard in 1972, and it is breed number 283 in Group 9.
